**Personetics integrates Plaid open banking data to sharpen bank personalisation**

*The partnership gives banks and credit unions a combined view of on-us and off-us customer activity, sharpening the contest for account primacy as open finance widens the data pool.*

Personetics, an AI-driven banking personalisation platform, is integrating Plaid's open banking connectivity to offer financial institutions a fuller picture of customer finances through a single integration. The combined data set merges a bank's own transaction records with account information held at competing institutions, feeding Personetics' models that generate insights, alerts and product triggers.

The tie-up is pitched squarely at the account primacy problem. As open finance regulations widen data access, banks risk losing visibility of customers who spread balances and spending across multiple providers. By ingesting off-us data alongside proprietary records, banks can identify behavioural patterns, such as salary deposits shifting to a rival or recurring payments moving elsewhere, and respond with targeted engagement.

The integration reflects a broader pattern: banks treating open banking not just as a compliance obligation but as a competitive intelligence layer. It also illustrates how the personalisation market is converging with open finance infrastructure, turning data aggregation into a prerequisite for AI-driven customer engagement rather than a standalone service.

*Sources: [Personetics integrates Plaid open banking data to offer banks wider customer view](https://app.dealroom.co/news/feed/personetics-integrates-plaid-open-banking-data-to-offer-banks-wider-customer-view) — Dealroom | [Personetics integrates Plaid open banking data](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/personetics-integrates-plaid-open-banking-112241523.html) — Yahoo Finance | [Personetics partners with Plaid to help banks win account primacy with Open Finance](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/personetics-partners-with-plaid-to-help-banks-win-account-primacy-with-open-finance/) — Openbankingexpo | [Personetics Partners with Plaid to Help Banks Win Account Primacy with Open Finance Intelligence](https://glenbrook.com/payments_news/personetics-partners-with-plaid-to-help-banks-win-account-primacy-with-open-finance-intelligence/) — Glenbrook*

**Modulr becomes direct participant in CHAPS, settling at the Bank of England**

*Settling directly at the Bank of England removes the need for correspondent banking relationships and gives the payments platform end-to-end control over liquidity across all three core UK interbank schemes.*

Modulr has become a direct participant in CHAPS, the UK's same-day high-value payment system, enabling it to settle directly at the Bank of England. The change eliminates the need for an intermediary bank to process CHAPS transactions on its behalf.

Direct participation in CHAPS has historically been confined to a small group of major banks. Modulr, which holds an electronic money institution licence and is a founding shareholder of the UK Payments Initiative, already had direct access to Faster Payments and Bacs. Adding CHAPS completes its access to the three core UK interbank payment schemes, giving it end-to-end control over payment routing and settlement timing.

For Modulr's client base of platforms, fintechs and businesses that embed payments into their operations, direct CHAPS access means faster and more predictable settlement for high-value transactions. Non-bank payment firms securing direct clearing access remains uncommon, but each new entrant reinforces a gradual structural shift in how UK payment infrastructure is governed and accessed.

*Sources: [London Based Fintech Modulr Gains Direct Access To Major UK Payment Systems](https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2026/08/298858-london-based-fintech-modulr-gains-direct-access-to-major-uk-payment-systems/) — Crowdfundinsider | [Modulr becomes Chaps direct participant](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110686/modulr-becomes-chaps-direct-participant?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Midnite launches pay-by-bank deposits and withdrawals via TrueLayer**

*Gambling's emergence as a proving ground for pay-by-bank at scale gains another data point as open banking payments go live for both deposits and withdrawals on a UK sports betting platform.*

Midnite, a UK sports betting platform, is launching pay-by-bank for both deposits and withdrawals through TrueLayer's open banking infrastructure. The integration allows players to fund accounts and receive winnings directly from and to their bank accounts without entering card details.

Gambling has become one of the most active verticals for pay-by-bank adoption in the UK, driven by a combination of regulatory pressure and commercial incentive. The Gambling Commission's confirmation in July that financial risk assessments can use open banking data has given operators a reason to integrate the rails. For platforms like Midnite, pay-by-bank also reduces card processing fees and the chargebacks that are common in the sector.

TrueLayer has been building its position in gambling payments since launching its bank-on-file product. The intersection of open banking and gambling has drawn scrutiny from both consumer advocates concerned about affordability checks and industry bodies pushing back against them.

*Sources: [Midnite Adds TrueLayer Pay by Bank](https://igamingfuture.com/midnite-adds-truelayer-pay-by-bank/) — iGaming Future | [Sports betting platform Midnite launches Pay by Bank in the UK via TrueLayer](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/sports-betting-platform-midnite-launches-pay-by-bank-in-the-uk-via-truelayer/) — Openbankingexpo*

**UK mobile wallet registrations reach nearly two thirds of adults**

*Fresh industry data shows cards remain dominant but mobile wallet penetration has crossed a threshold that reshapes how banks and fintechs think about digital checkout.*

Nearly two thirds of UK adults are now registered with at least one mobile wallet provider, according to the latest industry data, though cards continue to dominate overall payment volumes. The figure marks a steady acceleration from the 57% reported in the previous data release.

The growth reflects both the normalisation of contactless NFC payments at the point of sale and the expansion of wallet functionality into online checkout, transit and in-app purchases. Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay account for the bulk of registrations, but the rising penetration creates competitive pressure on card networks and issuers to ensure their products are provisioned into wallets by default.

For pay-by-bank advocates, the data presents a mixed picture. Wallet adoption entrenches card-based payment habits at the point of sale, even as account-to-account alternatives gain traction in e-commerce and recurring payments. The challenge for open banking-based propositions is that wallet UX has set consumer expectations that direct bank payment flows have yet to match consistently.

*Sources: [Mobile wallets gain traction in the UK](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48268/mobile-wallets-gain-traction-in-the-uk?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
